page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is an accelerator-optimized virtual server configured for compute-heavy parallel workloads. The system features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supporting simultaneous multithreading and AVX-512 vector extensions. It includes 384 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace generation, providing 192 GB of aggregated video memory. Local storage is not included, requiring persistent network-attached storage for operating systems and runtime data.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution and high memory throughput, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics placing in the upper performance tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 208.49 GB/sec on uncached 256MB read tests and 94.37 GB/sec on writes. However, single-threaded processing reflects the modest 2.2 GHz base frequency, resulting in lower scores on single-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and file compression tasks. Redis operations perform strongly at 63.66 million operations per second, while general web serving throughput performs within average industry ranges.

Machine learning benchmarks highlight the architectural strengths of the eight L4 GPUs. Prompt processing throughput ranks in the top tier across varying model sizes, reaching 11350.23 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, 2692.08 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, and 294.28 tokens per second on 70B models. Text generation throughput remains robust, maintaining top-tier metrics on 7B models and strong performance on 70B architectures.

From a resource and infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance balances extensive GPU compute density with standard general-purpose host memory. While the lower per-core single-threaded throughput represents a tradeoff for serial operations, the multi-GPU topology maximizes throughput for horizontally parallel tasks. Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is best aligned with large language model serving, real-time video transcoding, distributed model evaluation, and graphics rendering farms.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a GPU-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs, 48 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.2 GHz, 384 GB of system RAM, and eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs delivering a combined 192 GB of VRAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hardware AVX-512 extensions, the instance provides high-throughput parallel compute and substantial memory bandwidth. While single-thread benchmarks indicate lower per-core execution speeds, the system demonstrates high multi-core throughput and top-tier performance in language model prompt processing and inference. The configuration lacks bundled local storage, requiring external storage volumes for disk operations. Resource allocation maintains a balanced 4 GB of memory per vCPU, making the hardware density cost-efficient for scaled, multi-GPU tasks without overprovisioning host memory. The platform is engineered for distributed machine learning inference, real-time video transcoding, parallel graphics rendering, and memory-intensive artificial intelligence serving pipelines.
